title: Delegated Shedding Policy with Grace Epochs and Per-Region Locality
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a hybrid admission control pattern where global edge routers delegate fine-grained shedding decisions to lightweight per-region locality controllers. Each controller enforces a small set of policies (priority lanes, soft quotas, and grace epochs) that allow progressive fidelity degradation instead of hard drops. This ticket implements the policy, runtime hooks, and observability for rollout.
background: We currently perform global admission decisions at the ingress layer which leads to blunt, tenant-wide drops during cross-region spikes. This causes noisy customer impact and hamstrings graceful degradations (partial responses, reduced token budgets). The team has prototypes focused on lane-based shedding but lacks a coordinated delegation model with time-bounded grace behavior per request.
goals: 1) Reduce hard-fail client errors during regional overloads by 40% for P1 tenants. 2) Provide per-region controllers that can degrade fidelity progressively (3 defined fidelity modes) within configurable grace epochs. 3) Expose metrics and runbook for SLO-driven rollout and rollback.
non_goals: This ticket does not change model selection or kernel-level quantization recommendations. It also does not implement billing changes for partial responses.
proposed_solution: Add a Delegated Shedding API on the ingress plane: when the global router sees elevated load, it tags requests with a delegation token and forwards them to the regional locality controller. The controller applies tenant-weighted priority queues, a soft admission window (probabilistic admission), and a grace epoch timer (default 1500ms) during which it attempts degraded-but-functional responses (shorter context, streaming partial outputs, or structured summary fallbacks). If the grace epoch expires without capacity, it issues a best-effort denial with structured fallbacks and CRB (circuit breaker) annotations.
policy_kinds:
- Priority lanes: realtime, interactive, background
- Soft quotas: probabilistic admission percentages per lane
- Grace epochs: short time windows allowing progressive fallback
- Circuit breaker hooks: trip thresholds based on regional CPU/GPU queue length and tail latency
tradeoffs:
- Delegation adds a hop and slight metadata overhead; mitigated by lightweight protobuf token and cache.
- Local controllers increase operational surface; we constrain them to stateless policies and use control-plane reconciliation.
- Probabilistic admission can be non-deterministic for a single tenant; we provide deterministic modes for enterprise customers.
implementation_steps: Add DelegationToken header and contract in API spec
Implement Regional Locality Controller service with HTTP/GRPC endpoint (policy apply + decision)
Wire ingress router to call controller asynchronously with 8ms budget and fallback to local static policy
Add fidelity degradation hooks in runtime: max_tokens cap, summarized response handler, and partial stream truncation
Instrument metrics: delegated_decisions, grace_epoch_hit_rate, fidelity_mode_distribution, per-tenant dropped_tokens
Create e2e canary that routes a subset of requests from staging to new controller
Author runbook and circuit-breaker tuning knobs in Console
acceptance_criteria: Ingress successfully attaches DelegationToken and falls back to static policy when controller times out
Regional controller responds within 8ms P95 under nominal load for small policy sets
Grace epoch behavior demonstrated in canary: at least one progressive fallback path per overcapacity event
Dashboards show reduction in hard 5xx errors during simulated regional spike by >= 40% for targeted tenants
Security review completed and data plane tokens are KMS-encrypted in transit
testing_plan: Unit tests for DelegationToken lifecycle, integration tests for ingress-controller RPC timeouts, chaos test that introduces regional GPU starvation and validates graceful fallbacks, and load test at 3x nominal traffic to exercise probabilistic admission behavior. QA checklist will include deterministic-mode verification for enterprise tenants.
rollout_plan: 1) Deploy controller to staging region and run synthetic traffic job for 48h. 2) Canary 1% traffic in us-west with monitoring and auto-rollback threshold. 3) Increment to 10% after 24h if error budget stable. 4) Full rollout to region if SLOs hold for 72h. 5) Repeat per-region with staggered start times.
monitoring_and_alerting: Create alerts for: regional_controller_latency_p95 > 20ms, grace_epoch_expiry_rate > 5% over 10m, fidelity_mode_shift_sudden_change, delegated_denials_increase > 2x baseline. Wire alert to oncall runbook with immediate rollback steps.
status_updates: 2026-02-12: Spike completed. Prototype controller handles 500rps with 4ms avg decision latency.
2026-02-25: Design review feedback: make grace epoch configurable per-route and add enterprise deterministic mode.
2026-03-03: Security review kickoff; data-in-transit token encryption validated by Security team.
2026-03-10: Integration tests passing in staging; canary scheduled for 2026-03-15
qa_results: Integration + chaos tests green in staging. Observed 48% reduction in hard 5xx for test tenant under synthetic regional spike during canary simulation.
follow_ups:
- Add automatic per-tenant backpressure credits in a follow-up ticket.
- Explore multi-controller consensus for cross-region coordinated shedding as phase 2.
notes_for_release: Enable feature flag 'delegated_shedding' per-region. Default to off for existing production regions until canary validated.
post_deployment_checks: Verify delegated_decisions P95 < 10ms, grace_epoch_expiry_rate < 1%, reduce customer-visible 5xxs for impacted tenants.

communication_plan: Pre-signed customer advisory for enterprise tenants, in-console banner for early adopters, and internal doc shared to Solutions and Support teams.
final_notes: This approach prioritizes progressive user experience over blunt availability cuts. It requires careful tuning of probabilistic admission and conservative canary thresholds to avoid oscillation.
